clue.text: Joins in practice in case of foreigners

indicators.note: practice placed in the case means it sits within the outer shell of the next word
the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: to practise something is to use it, so practice can stand for use

explanation.surface: A practising expat joins in with other foreigners in some shared case.
explanation.walkthrough: Of the two 'in's, only the one before 'case of' signals containment; the earlier one is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To fuse two things is to melt or merge them together, a synonym for joins.

clue.text: One hunted for a short while?

explanation.surface: A riddle about a hunted man who is only on the run briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: A runaway is pursued by the law; the adjective also means fleeting, lasting only a brief time.

clue.text: At the end of the day, tabloid's depressed

definitions.text: At the end of the day

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
someone depressed is feeling down

explanation.surface: By evening, a popular newspaper is feeling gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: THE SUN is a British tabloid newspaper; the 's stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunset comes when the day is over, the close of daylight hours.

clue.text: Teacher with key for old address

parts.note: British schoolchildren address a male teacher as sir
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A teacher holding a key to some old house address.
explanation.walkthrough: British pupils call a male teacher 'Sir'.
explanation.definitionFit: This was an archaic respectful form for addressing a king or lord, hence an old title of address.

clue.text: Worn out by broken pride, etc

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so these letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone exhausted by wounded pride and all the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges PRIDE plus ETC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worn out by age or long use is feeble and dilapidated.

clue.text: Where ironing is an education?

parts.note: smoothing out creases is evening a cloth, and lessons are classes

explanation.surface: A question about a place where learning to iron counts as schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: To iron is to make cloth even, so a lesson in ironing is an 'evening class' in a punning sense; really these are adult-education sessions held after work.
explanation.definitionFit: Adult courses held after working hours are a common form of further education.

clue.text: Got up to find top of stove covered in egg

indicators.note: the letter is wrapped inside the egg word, enclosed within it

parts.note: roe is fish eggs

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone rose to find the cooker smeared with egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top of' takes S from 'stove'; 'covered in' puts it inside ROE.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of rise: someone who stood or climbed out of bed did so.

clue.text: The sort of person who might put Iran in trouble

indicators.note: letters in trouble are in disarray, so they are jumbled into a new word

explanation.surface: A remark about the type of figure who might cause difficulties for Iran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges PUT plus IRAN. The definition is loose: the clue implies a strict, moralising sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A strait-laced moralist with severe religious views is one particular sort of person.

clue.text: Royal family study form, dismissing outsiders

indicators.note: dropping the outsiders of each word leaves only their inner letters

explanation.surface: A study of the form of the royal family, minus the fringe members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing outsiders' strips the first and last letters of 'study' and 'form', leaving TUD and OR.
explanation.definitionFit: The House founded by Henry VII ruled England from 1485 to 1603, a royal dynasty.

clue.text: Some banks are emptying theatres!

explanation.surface: A remark that certain banks are clearing out the playhouses.
explanation.definitionFit: Financial institutions that settle cheques between banks; read literally, playhouses being vacated after a show.

clue.text: Common Latin types left

parts.note: genera is the Latin plural of genus, a type or class

explanation.surface: Ordinary Latin categories have been abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Something common is widespread and usual, the same idea as broadly applying to most.

clue.text: Guaranteed to be definitely in the final

indicators.note: the word for definitely is placed in the word for the final, within it

parts.note: the final part of something is its end
sure as an adverb means definitely, as in 'sure, I'll come'

explanation.surface: A team is certain to make it to the cup final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the final' suggests a cup final, but here it just means an end.
explanation.definitionFit: To have made certain of something is to have secured or assured it.

clue.text: Clip youngster crossing river

indicators.note: the child word stretches across the river letter, holding it within

parts.note: a tot is a small child
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Giving a child a clip round the ear as they wade across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clip' suggests a smack; here it means a brisk pace, as in 'at a fair clip'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast pace, between a walk and a run, is a jog or clip.

clue.text: Mad artist made an offer

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
to bid is to make an offer at auction

explanation.surface: A crazed painter put in a bid at auction.
explanation.definitionFit: Crazed or frenzied, like an animal with the disease that causes madness.

clue.text: Take the lead from the beginning, but tail off

indicators.note: taking the tail off removes the final letter of the word

parts.note: the beginning of something is its start

explanation.surface: Advice to lead from the front at the outset but then ease off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail off' cuts the last T from START.
explanation.definitionFit: To play the leading role in a show is to headline it.

clue.text: We hear when to select the lavender

indicators.note: what we hear is a word spoken, so the sound of the phrase matters, not its spelling

parts.note: as means when, and to select is to pick: as pick

explanation.surface: Being told the right moment to choose lavender.
explanation.walkthrough: AS (when) plus PICK (select), spoken, gives the plant name. Aspic, or spike lavender, is a lavender species.
explanation.definitionFit: Spike lavender, Lavandula latifolia, is also known by this name: a specific kind of the plant.

clue.text: Lesson taught by end of term exam

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A lesson learned through an end-of-term exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' takes M from 'term'.
explanation.definitionFit: The teaching message drawn from a story or event is the lesson it imparts.

clue.text: Fielder disappearing from view?

parts.note: a cricket fielding position, point, that is vanishing, read as the spot where lines in a picture fade out of sight

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder drifting out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: POINT is a fielding position in cricket; one that is disappearing is 'vanishing'. Really the term is the spot in perspective drawing where parallel lines seem to meet.
explanation.definitionFit: In perspective drawing, the spot where receding parallel lines converge and objects fade out of sight.

clue.text: Worried about aid? Get at its distribution

indicators.note: distributing letters spreads them out, so they are rearranged here

explanation.surface: Concern about aid money: go after how it is handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distribution' rearranges AID plus GET AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone worried is anxious and unsettled, nervously stirred up.

clue.text: Sweeping reforms from the house bound?

definitions.text: Sweeping reforms from the house bound?

parts.words: Sweeping reforms from the house bound?
parts.note: sweeping and tidying a home thoroughly, with bound hinting at the season of leaping into action

explanation.surface: Radical changes brought in by someone stuck at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweeping reforms' suggests politics; it is literal broom work. 'bound' is a leap, hinting at the season, while 'house' gives the setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorough annual tidy of the home, traditionally done in the season after winter.

clue.text: Quietly speak in support of exercises and thus give encouragement?

definitions.note: the definition is a verb phrase; the answer is the noun for a rousing speech one gives to encourage

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece in support of another sits under it, so it comes after

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
to speak is to talk

explanation.surface: A coach quietly says something to support training and so cheer people on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in support of' places P plus TALK beneath PE in the down entry. The definition is loose: this is a speech given to encourage.
explanation.definitionFit: A rousing speech meant to boost morale, the kind a coach makes before a match.

clue.text: One thus excludes lines under pressure

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
so means thus, in that way
to bar someone is to exclude them

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps people out while under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under pressure' looks like stress; on a weather map these lines join points of equal air pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: On weather charts, these contours connect points of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Manage to find work in church

indicators.note: the work word goes in the church word, within it

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Getting by with a job in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: A cope is also a priest's cloak, so 'work in church' reads like a definition; it is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To deal successfully with difficulty is to handle or get by.

clue.text: Simple machine for trapping this flipping creature

annotationWithheld.why: Simple machine for trapping this flipping creature (5) for CAMEL: no simple machine word found that, holding ME or reversed, gives CAMEL; clue confirmed as printed but parse not found
annotationWithheld.clue: Simple machine for trapping this flipping creature

clue.text: A device for lifting one trapped by the crowd

indicators.note: the one letter is trapped by the crowd word, held inside it

parts.note: a host is a great crowd, as in a host of angels
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lifting gadget with someone stuck in it amid a throng.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapped by' puts I inside HOST.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulley or winch apparatus raises heavy loads; a crane-like device.

clue.text: Most of the way to an overwhelming victory

indicators.note: most of a word is all of it but its last letter

parts.note: a route is a way to a place

explanation.surface: Being almost there on the road to a crushing win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops the final E of ROUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A crushing defeat inflicted on an enemy is a decisive win for the other side.

clue.text: Hard knock for a follower with depression

parts.note: B is what follows the letter a in the alphabet
a low is an area of low atmospheric pressure, a depression

explanation.surface: A tough setback for a supporter who is feeling down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a follower' is the letter B, which comes after A; 'follower' tempts one toward fan or disciple.
explanation.definitionFit: A setback or shock, as well as a physical strike, is a hard knock.

clue.text: A shot in the dark causing wound

explanation.surface: A random strike in the darkness that leaves an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild guess, as in 'have a go'; and as a verb, to pierce with a knife.

clue.text: The compiler — fool to catch the French disease!

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as the compiler, so me

indicators.note: the fool word catches the French article, holding it inside

parts.note: an ass is a fool
le is French for the

explanation.surface: The setter, a fool, picking up the French disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The French disease' is an old euphemism for syphilis, which steers away from the real illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A contagious viral illness causing a red rash, common in childhood.

clue.text: A minor actor to court and take out

parts.note: an extra is a minor actor in a crowd scene

explanation.surface: A bit-part player taking someone to court and then out.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull or remove something, such as a tooth, is to draw it out.

clue.text: Too fond of sage?

parts.note: to like something is to be fond of it
a sage person is wise

explanation.surface: A question about loving the herb sage too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sage' suggests the herb; it means wise. 'Too' means also, not excessively.
explanation.definitionFit: Also, in the same way, as a reply agreeing to the same.

clue.text: Located when asleep?

annotationWithheld.why: Located when asleep? (5) for BASED: AS (when) inside BED, but 'asleep' would be both BED and the containment signal, one word doing two jobs
